subject: Re: ACME feature parity — streaming & tool-calls next tests
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Bob Li <bob.li@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME discovery follow-up / feature parity tests

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for running through the discovery with us yesterday — helpful conversation. Our engineering and platform teams want to validate a few items before we can move to a pilot:

- Streaming responses (we have low-latency chat flows and need partial responses streamed)
- Tool/function calling (we need the model to reliably call external tools, with structured JSON arguments)
- Structured outputs (schema'd JSON outputs for entity extraction and reranking)

Can you confirm Redwood can produce short-term test endpoints for these three areas, and share a suggested test plan? We can run tests against an internal harness and share metrics.

Also, our security team will need a short list of what telemetry/logs are available during the tests.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Chen
Director, AI Platform
ACME Corp

--
Alice Chen
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@acme.com>, Bob Li <bob.li@acme.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME discovery follow-up / feature parity tests

Hi Alice — great to meet you and Bob yesterday. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

Recap:
- Redwood supports streaming partial responses, structured outputs, and function/tool calling. We have streaming endpoints and a function-calling contract that returns JSON-compatible args; we also provide structured output helpers and validators for schema enforcement.

Proposed test plan (attached as a CSV and a short matrix PDF):
1) Streaming: two scenarios — (a) short chat streaming (avg 30 tokens/sec) and (b) long-generation streaming (token bursts). Measure latency to first token and total completion time.
2) Function/Tool calling: 10 representative tool schemas (sample payloads included). Validation: correctness of arguments, number of retries, and how we expose call metadata.
3) Structured outputs: run 5 schema types (entities, addresses, invoices, QA pairs, rerank lists). Compare Redwood vs Hyperscaler X on exact-match/validation pass rates.

What Redwood will provide:
- Temporary test endpoints (staging) with an API key.
- A test harness spec (CSV attached) and expected payloads.
- A telemetry summary doc for security (logs, request/response metadata, KV cache behavior, request IDs).

Attachments: acme_streaming_test_plan.csv (test cases), redwood_feature-parity-matrix.pdf (high-level comparison matrix)

Proposed timeline:
- Tests provisioned by Tue 13 Apr
- ACME runs tests Wed–Thu 14–15 Apr
- Review call Fri 16 Apr

If that works, I’ll loop in our infra/engineering resources.

Best,
Marissa Cole

marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: ACME discovery follow-up / feature parity tests

Team — forwarding ACME’s ask and the test plan attachments. High level: they want streaming, tool-calls, structured outputs validated vs hyperscaler. Can we support provisioning staging endpoints and a short-lived test key?

Action items I’m proposing:
- Dev: provision streaming-enabled staging endpoints and ensure function-calling contract is enabled + logs for call metadata. We may need a slightly higher kv-cache window for streaming tests. (see attachment)
- Dylan: prepare a quick comparison harness that will run Redwood and Hyperscaler X against the same payloads and compute latency, first-token, validation pass-rate.
- Naomi: own the test run coordination and timing with ACME; confirm security telemetry doc is sufficient.

Constraints/notes:
- If quantized models change behavior for function args, call that out with examples. We need deterministic behavior for structured outputs.
- Keep endpoints internal (staging) — do not expose in public docs.

I’ll be on the 16 Apr review call with ACME — need a short slide that summarizes test infra and known limitations.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 07:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: ACME discovery follow-up / feature parity tests

Sounds good — I’ll start provisioning the staging endpoints today. Quick technical notes:
- Streaming: we’ll enable chunked responses and instrument first-packet timing. For long-gen streaming we may need to tune kernel selection to avoid tail latency spikes.
- Function calling: need the sample schemas (CSV has basics) — please confirm any nested JSON edge cases; quantization can occasionally alter tokenization around braces/commas which affects arg parsing.
- Structured outputs: we’ll run the validator against both quantized and fp16 variants to surface regressions.

Marissa — can you share 2–3 sample payloads from ACME (or I can use the CSV samples)? Also, do we want to run a small QPS test (10–20 qps) to surface reliability issues?

--
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
